research_questions: How much of the TA@10 gap between the paper's PCA-256/INT8 cut and exact target reconstruction is codec loss, and what is the fidelity-storage frontier of the post-vision cut?
How is raw target-build time split between CPU preprocessing, the visual prefix, and the language-model suffix, and does that split predict the measured replay saving?
calibration: Same split as sigir-version-evolution-matrix-v1: numpy RandomState(0) reserves 30% of documents as the holdout; the first 64 sorted non-holdout documents fit one query-free PCA basis of rank 512 from 8192 uniformly sampled visual tokens. Lower ranks truncate that nested basis.

evaluation.reference: target_full: exact v0.2 documents encoded from raw pages

predictions_frozen_before_output.bf16: TA@10 = 1.0 up to floating-point nondeterminism; any deviation is a bug in the replay path, not a codec effect.
predictions_frozen_before_output.monotone: TA@10 is non-increasing as payload bytes per page shrink along int8 -> int4 -> pca512 -> pca256 -> pca128 -> pca64.
predictions_frozen_before_output.leverage: cut_leverage on arxivqa/docvqa is >= 0.8 and on flickr is lower because natural images produce fewer visual tokens; measured replay saving must not exceed leverage.
predictions_frozen_before_output.indomain_bridges: In-domain bridges may raise nDCG slightly over stale but will not approach the TA@10 of any post-vision codec, because query-side alignment cannot recover document-side MaxSim evidence.

claim_boundary: One transition, one backbone, single-GPU timings with image batch size 1 as in the paper. Fidelity numbers describe the holdout ranking against the exact target index, not qrel effectiveness in general.
compatibility_baselines: Procrustes and affine ridge (lambda 0.01) bridges from target-version query tokens to legacy query tokens, fitted in-domain on the non-holdout 70% queries of the same corpus; evaluated against the legacy (stale) document bank. This removes the cross-domain (Energy-fitted) handicap of the paper's bridges.
